paragraphs.title: David's Desire to Build a House for God and God's Response

answers: Rest from all his enemies
A larger army
A new palace
easy.explanation: The passage says that the LORD had given David rest round about from all his enemies.
easy.q: What had the LORD given David before David spoke about building a house for Him?

answers: Saul
Nathan the prophet
The captain of his army
easy.explanation: David told Nathan the prophet that he dwelt in a house of cedar while the ark was in curtains.
easy.q: To whom did David speak about his desire to build a house for God?

answers: In a house of cedar
In the king's palace
Within curtains
easy.explanation: David said, “the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.”
easy.q: Where did the ark of God dwell?

answers: He lived in a house of cedar while the ark dwelt in curtains
Nathan commanded him to build it
His enemies required him to build it
medium.explanation: David noticed the contrast between his house of cedar and the tent-like dwelling of the ark.
medium.q: Why did David want to build a house for the LORD?

answers: He immediately opposed it
He agreed and told David to do what was in his heart
He told David to wait many years
medium.explanation: Nathan initially said, “Go, do all that is in thine heart.”
medium.q: What was Nathan's first response to David's plan?

answers: God's dwelling with Israel in a tent
David's military travels
The building of Solomon's palace
medium.explanation: The LORD explained that He had not dwelt in a permanent house but had been with Israel in a tent and tabernacle.
medium.q: What does the expression “have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle” describe?

answers: Nathan first agreed, but the LORD explained that David was not the one required to build the house
Nathan first opposed it, but the LORD commanded David to build immediately
Nathan forgot David's request, and the LORD ignored it
challenge.explanation: Nathan initially approved David's plan, but the LORD later gave him a different message.
challenge.q: What changed between Nathan's first response and the LORD's message that night?

answers: A house of cedar was not a condition of serving God
Israel's leaders did not know the LORD
Israel had never lived in tents
challenge.explanation: The LORD says He never asked any of Israel's judges or leaders, “Why build ye not me an house of cedar?”
challenge.q: What point does the LORD make by saying that He had never commanded Israel's leaders to build Him a house of cedar?

answers: David's house of cedar versus the LORD's tent and tabernacle
Nathan versus Saul
Israel versus Egypt
challenge.explanation: David lived in a house of cedar, while the ark was associated with a tent and tabernacle.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in this passage?

paragraphs.title: God's Promises to David and Israel

answers: From the king's house
From the sheepcote and following the sheep
From Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The LORD reminded David that He had taken him from the sheepcote and from following the sheep.
easy.q: From where did the LORD take David?

answers: A prophet
A judge
A ruler over Israel
easy.explanation: The LORD took David from the sheep to be ruler over His people Israel.
easy.q: What did the LORD make David?

answers: Appoint them a place where they could dwell securely
Send them back to Egypt
Replace their king
easy.explanation: The LORD promised to appoint a place for Israel and plant them so they would move no more.
easy.q: What did the LORD promise to do for Israel?

answers: From priesthood to kingship
From shepherding sheep to ruling Israel
From Egypt to the wilderness
medium.explanation: David was taken from following the sheep to become ruler over Israel.
medium.q: How does the LORD describe David's journey?

answers: He was with David and cut off his enemies
He built the temple for David
He removed David from Israel
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest,” and cut off David's enemies.
medium.q: What did the LORD do for David throughout his journey?

answers: A leader or sovereign
A shepherd of sheep
A household servant
medium.explanation: The LORD appointed David to lead and govern His people Israel.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “ruler” mean?

answers: Israel would receive security, and David would receive an enduring royal dynasty
Israel would receive a new king, and David would leave the land
Israel would receive a new tent, and David would become a shepherd again
challenge.explanation: The LORD promised both stability for Israel and a royal house for David.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the promise of a place for Israel and the promise of a house for David?

answers: The LORD would build David a physical residence
The LORD would establish David's royal family and dynasty
David would build a house for the ark
challenge.explanation: The promised house refers to David's continuing royal line, not merely to a building.
challenge.q: What does the expression “he will make thee an house” mean in this context?

answers: Instead of David building a house for the LORD, the LORD promises to make David a house
David abandons his plan, and the LORD commands him to build a palace
The LORD promises that Israel will build only a house for David
challenge.explanation: The LORD responds to David's desire by promising to establish a house, or dynasty, for David.
challenge.q: How is David's original plan turned around in this passage?

paragraphs.title: The Promise of the Dynasty and Royal House

answers: David's seed
Nathan
One of David's enemies
easy.explanation: The LORD promised to set up David's seed after David's days were fulfilled.
easy.q: Whom did the LORD promise to set up after David?

answers: A new city
A house for the LORD's name
A military camp
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “He shall build an house for my name.”

answers: The LORD would be his father
The LORD would be his enemy
The LORD would not know him
easy.explanation: The LORD said, “I will be his father, and he shall be my son.”
easy.q: What relationship would the LORD have with David's son?

answers: He would be chastened with the rod of men and the stripes of the children of men
He would immediately lose all Israel
He would become ruler over other nations
medium.explanation: The LORD described discipline and chastening if David's son committed iniquity.
medium.q: What would happen if David's son committed iniquity?

answers: His mercy would not depart from him
He would never be disciplined
He would immediately cease to be king
medium.explanation: The LORD promised, “my mercy shall not depart away from him.”
medium.q: What did the LORD promise despite the possibility that the son might sin?

answers: Only until the end of his life
For ever
Until an enemy arrived
medium.explanation: The passage repeatedly says that the throne and kingdom would be established for ever.
medium.q: How long would the throne of David's son's kingdom be established?

answers: Sin brings chastening, but the LORD's covenant mercy toward David's house is not removed
Sin is not counted, so no punishment is needed
Mercy ends the kingdom and replaces it with another one
challenge.explanation: The passage includes both discipline for iniquity and continuing mercy toward David's royal line.
challenge.q: How can punishment for sin exist together with mercy that does not depart?

answers: David wanted to build a house for the LORD, while the LORD promised David a royal house and dynasty
David wanted a house for his son, while the LORD promised a house for the ark
There is no difference between them
challenge.explanation: David's plan concerned a building for God, but God's promise concerned David's continuing royal family.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the house David wanted to build and the house the LORD promised him?

answers: The continuing nature of David's kingdom and dynasty
A short limit on the kingdom
Israel's wandering in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the enduring establishment of David's throne and house.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated phrase “for ever” in this passage?

paragraphs.title: David's Prayer of Gratitude and Wonder

answers: Before the LORD
At the city gate
In Nathan's house
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD.”
easy.q: Where did David sit after hearing the LORD's words?

answers: The greatness and goodness shown to him and his house
The strength of his enemies
The number of Israel's cities
easy.explanation: David marveled that the LORD had brought him so far and had spoken concerning his house for a great while to come.

answers: As a people redeemed by God and made special to Him
As a people who had not been redeemed
As a people with no relationship to God
easy.explanation: David described Israel as the people whom God redeemed for Himself and made a name.

answers: Wonder and humility before God's goodness
Anger about the LORD's promise
A desire to leave the kingdom
medium.explanation: David humbly wondered why he and his house had received such favor.
medium.q: What does David's question, “Who am I, O Lord GOD?” express?

answers: His greatness and uniqueness
The building of David's house of cedar
David's personal wealth
medium.explanation: David says there is none like the LORD and no God beside Him.
medium.q: For what does David praise the LORD?

answers: God redeemed Israel, made them His people, and became their God
God drove Israel away from Himself
Israel chose a king without any connection to God
medium.explanation: David speaks of Israel as the people God redeemed and confirmed as His own.
medium.q: What relationship between the LORD and Israel does David describe?

answers: In both cases, he emphasizes that their greatness and identity come from God
He praises only himself and does not mention Israel
He compares Israel with David's enemies
challenge.explanation: David credits the LORD with both the blessings given to him and the special status given to Israel.
challenge.q: How is David's confession about himself connected with his confession about Israel?

answers: He approaches God with humility, reverence, and wonder
He is preparing to go to war
He is waiting for Nathan to build the house
challenge.explanation: David's posture and words introduce a prayer marked by humility and gratitude.
challenge.q: What can be learned from David's sitting before the LORD before praying?

answers: Israel's unique identity among the nations
Israel's complete lack of unity
Israel's lack of a history
challenge.explanation: David presents Israel as a people specially redeemed and formed by God.
challenge.q: What does David's description of Israel as “one nation in the earth” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: David's Request for Fulfillment and Blessing

answers: The word spoken concerning His servant and his house
The house of David's enemies
Nathan's tent
easy.explanation: David asked the LORD to establish His spoken word concerning David and his house for ever.
easy.q: What did David ask the LORD to establish for ever?

answers: The LORD's name
Saul's name
The names of David's enemies
easy.explanation: David prayed, “let thy name be magnified for ever.”
easy.q: What did David ask to be magnified for ever?

answers: That the LORD bless the house of His servant for ever
That the LORD remove his house
That the LORD give him new enemies
easy.explanation: David asked the LORD to bless his house so that it might continue for ever.
easy.q: What did David ask at the end of his prayer?

answers: The LORD had revealed His promise concerning David's house
Nathan had commanded him to pray
David did not believe the LORD's words
medium.explanation: David says that the LORD revealed His promise, and therefore he found it in his heart to pray.
medium.q: Why did David find it in his heart to pray this prayer?

answers: They are true
They are only secret sayings
They cannot be fulfilled
medium.explanation: David declares, “thou art that God, and thy words be true.”
medium.q: What did David say about the LORD's words?

answers: David asks for the blessing because the LORD Himself made the promise
The blessing depends on the strength of David's enemies
The blessing has no connection to the promise
medium.explanation: David bases his request on the fact that the LORD had spoken the promise.
medium.q: How is David's request for blessing connected to the LORD's words?

answers: David trusts the truth of God's word and asks Him to fulfill it
David completely doubts the promise
David wants to change what God said
challenge.explanation: David appeals to God's own promise and asks for its fulfillment.
challenge.q: What does the request “do as thou hast said” reveal about David's faith?

answers: He asks that God's name be magnified and that David's house be established before Him
He places David's house above God's name
He asks that only his own house be remembered
challenge.explanation: David's prayer joins the honoring of God's name with the establishment of his house before God.
challenge.q: What connection does David make between the greatness of God's name and the house of David?

answers: With gratitude, faith in God's word, and a request for continuing blessing
With anger because he would not build the house
By giving up his house and kingdom
challenge.explanation: David responds by praising God, trusting His promise, and asking Him to bless his house for ever.
challenge.q: How does David's prayer summarize his response to the promise?
